title: Add Request ID & Structured Logging Middleware
description: Introduces a lightweight middleware that generates a unique request ID for every incoming request, attaches it to the request object, adds it to the response header, and logs request/response details in a structured format. This improves traceability, debugging, and observability in production environments.
testCases: Middleware attaches a UUID v4 request ID to req.id and sets X-Request-Id header on the response
Middleware logs a JSON object containing method, url, status, duration, and request ID for successful requests
Middleware correctly logs error responses and includes the request ID
Middleware does not interfere with routes that do not call next() (e.g., early response)
acceptance: When the server receives any HTTP request, a unique request ID is generated, added to req.id, sent back in the X-Request-Id header, and a structured log entry is emitted containing method, url, status, duration, and the request ID. The middleware must work with async route handlers, not alter response bodies, and must not break existing functionality.
reason: Observability is critical for production-ready services. A request‑ID based logging system enables correlation across distributed logs, speeds up incident response, and meets common compliance requirements without adding external dependencies.
